A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSP-UAP research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet fooling-rate experiments for PSP-UAP, including transferability comparisons, component ablations, and appendix sensitivity studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds defense evaluations, additional architecture comparisons, and training-subset hyperparameter results.

M1.justification: The sampling procedure, transformations, inverse-KL reweighting, overall loss, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Although v2 explicitly inserts transformations into Equations (5)–(6), v1 Figure 2 already applies them before reweighting. Likewise, cropping noise plus UAP was already specified by v1 Equations (3)–(4). These clarify the documented procedure rather than establish a method change.

E1.justification: ImageNet classification remains the dataset and task. v2 adds evaluation with JPEG-compressed inputs in Table 7, introducing a distinct input-condition scenario. The additional ImageNet training subset changes split and sample usage rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The transformation study expands from the TRM-UAP comparison in v1 Figure 6 to GD-UAP and TRM-UAP component combinations in v2 Figure 5. GD-UAP already appeared in v1 Table 1 but newly participates in this particular comparison. The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds ConvNeXt-B, DeiT3, and ensemble-adversarial model configurations, plus a separately reported hyperparameter sweep on 1,000 randomly selected ImageNet training images. Existing perturbation bounds, iteration budget, selected hyperparameters, and fooling-rate metric remain unchanged. The new tuning account does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens diagnostic evaluation: Figure 5 tests whether the components benefit two baseline methods, Table 7 tests resistance to JPEG compression and adversarially trained defenses, and Figure 11 adds training-subset sensitivity curves. Existing component, epsilon, temperature, and validation-set hyperparameter analyses are retained or reorganized.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five runs in Table 2. No new run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is introduced. The added point estimates do not establish a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the temperature tables retain their values, but substantial new findings appear in v2 Figure 5, Tables 7–8, and the training-subset curves. For example, new JPEG tests report 58.61% versus 39.94% for PSP-UAP versus TRM on ResNet152; new DeiT3 white-box results are 9.54% versus 6.73%. These are additional settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations (5)–(6) change from f(x_n) and f(x_n + delta_t) to f(T(x_n)) and f(T(x_n + delta_t)). This corrects the formal distributions used for KL weighting to agree with the existing pipeline. The remaining mathematical framework is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: pseudo-semantic priors from UAPs, hard-sample reweighting, input transformations, and strong CNN attack transferability. Reordered contributions and rewritten wording do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the expanded component study as evidence that the approach is reusable across baseline methods. It adds limited ViT effectiveness as an applicability boundary, attributes this to the methods' CNN-oriented design, and suggests sample imbalance as an explanation for weaker N = 1 training-subset results. Existing white-box and visual-artifact limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix D promises public code after acceptance and states that supplementary code is supplied; v2 removes that section and provides a repository link in the abstract. v2 also documents the 1,000-image training-subset tuning procedure. These are access and reproducibility disclosures; repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for input-transformation defenses, ConvNeXt, DeiT III, and ensemble adversarial training. It also positions PSP components as enhancements applicable to GD-UAP and TRM-UAP. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, portions of the introduction, and conclusion are rewritten. Input Transformation moves before Sample Reweighting in Sections 3.3–3.4, with corresponding contribution reordering. Appendix paragraphs are reorganized and acknowledgements added, while the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Several displays are substantially reorganized: v1 Figures 7 and 12 are combined in v2 Figure 6, the transformation comparison is redesigned, two tables and training-subset plots are added, and galleries and temperature tables move. New labeling errors appear: Figure 7 reverses model names relative to identical appendix images, and Figure 6 labels the swept scaling bound beta_low despite its fixed value of 0.8.

improvement.justification: The added defense and component tests strengthen empirical scrutiny, while Table 8 and Appendix C clarify weak ViT performance. Corrected weighting equations and explicit tuning-data information improve transparency. These gains are partly offset by new model and scale-label errors in Figures 6–7 and sparse defense-protocol details. The net improvement is limited, with the core method and benchmark results retained.
